response_text: To protect confidentiality, the Census Bureau spent a fixed, deliberately small amount of "privacy loss" on its unit-level statistics — a global budget of rho = 0.07 (roughly epsilon = 2.47 at delta = 10⁻¹⁰), meaning the published numbers carry enough statistical noise that no individual record can be reliably identified. That budget was divided across geographic levels, with the great majority going to mid-sized areas — about 43% to block groups and 36% to tracts — followed by blocks (12%) and counties (9%), and only about half a percent each to the state and national totals.
